verdict.rationale: Godot is MIT-licensed open source with published compilation instructions for every supported platform, so users can build and run the entire engine on their own machines. A runtime probe confirms a one-command local install whose binary runs headless for CI builds, exports, and scripted automation. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of building the engine from source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Godot is completely free and open source under the very permissive MIT license. No strings attached, no royalties, nothing.
See the official docs for compilation instructions for every supported platform.
You can distribute unmodified and changed versions of Godot Engine, even commercially and under a different license (including proprietary)
Godot installs keylessly from Homebrew (cask godot 4.7.2, '2D and 3D game engine') — one command to the binary that runs `godot --headless` for CI builds, exports, and scripted editor automation.
If you want to run a dedicated server for your project on a machine that doesn't have a GPU or display server available, you'll need to run Godot with the `headless` display server
